facts.statement: The researchers developed a new computer model called PM-BGAQAN to predict three different seizure states from brain and heart signals.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: The system uses a specific filter to reduce background noise in the recordings while keeping the important signal details.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: A second part of the model analyzes the signals to find patterns across different time scales and combines the brain and heart data.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: The model includes a component that accounts for uncertainty in the data to make the features more reliable.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: An optimization algorithm was used to fine-tune the network settings for better performance.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: The model was tested on two existing datasets: one containing scalp EEG recordings and another containing wearable EEG and ECG data.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: The goal was to classify the signals into three states: before a seizure, during a seizure, and between seizures.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: The model achieved an overall accuracy of 99.86 percent in its tests.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: When tested on data from people not used in the training phase, the model reached an average accuracy of 98.06 percent.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: The authors suggest the model is an effective strategy for predicting seizure states from combined brain and heart signals.
